title: Pot odds, α, MDF, SPR
description: Eight questions on the four core betting formulas. Use a calculator only if you must.

questions.prompt: Villain bets 50bb into a 100bb pot. To call profitably, what minimum equity do you need (in %)?
questions.explanation: Required equity = C / (P + C) = 50 / (100 + 50) = 33.33%. Anything above this and the call is +EV against villain's range.

questions.prompt: You river-bluff 30bb into a 60bb pot. What is α (in %), the fold frequency required to break even?
questions.explanation: α = B / (P + B) = 30 / (60 + 30) = 33.33%. Note this is the same formula as pot odds when C = B.

questions.prompt: Facing a 75% pot bet, what is the defender's MDF (in %)?
questions.explanation: MDF = P / (P + B). With B = 0.75P, MDF = 1 / 1.75 ≈ 57.14%. Below this share of continues, opponent profits with any two cards.

questions.prompt: Which statement about pot odds and α is correct?

choices.text: Pot odds and α are different formulas; α uses the final pot in the denominator.
Pot odds is for the caller; α is for the bluffer; they share the formula B / (P + B) when C = B.
α is always larger than pot odds because the bluffer is risking more.

questions.explanation: When the call equals the bet, both reduce to B / (P + B). The number means different things — required equity vs required fold rate — but the algebra is identical.

questions.prompt: MDF is the equity threshold at which a defender should call. If they have less equity than MDF, they should fold.
questions.explanation: MDF is a *frequency* threshold, not an equity threshold. It says what fraction of the *range* must continue, assuming GTO bluffing by villain. Equity-based calling is governed by pot odds, not MDF.

questions.prompt: 100bb effective. CO opens 2.5bb, BB 3-bets to 9bb, CO calls. Compute the SPR at the start of the flop (round to 1 decimal).
questions.explanation: Flop pot = 9 + 9 + 0.5 (SB dead) = 18.5bb. Remaining effective stack ≈ 91bb. SPR ≈ 91 / 18.5 ≈ 4.9.

questions.prompt: At which SPR is top pair / strong overpair generally committing in the absence of further reads?

choices.text: SPR > 13 — deeper means more chances to extract value.
SPR 2–4 — shallow enough that two pot-sized bets get stacks in.
SPR < 0.5 — only when both players are basically pot-committed.
SPR doesn't affect commitment for one-pair hands.

questions.explanation: At SPR 2–4 the pot is shallow enough that a few normal-sized bets get all the money in. Top pair / overpair / strong draws are usually committing in this range.

questions.prompt: Which entries from the bet-size summary table are correct? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: 1/2 pot bet → caller needs 33.3% equity, defender's MDF 66.7%.
Pot-sized bet → caller needs 50% equity, defender's MDF 50%.
2× pot overbet → caller needs 60% equity, defender's MDF 40%.
1/3 pot bet → caller needs 25% equity, defender's MDF 75%.

questions.explanation: The 2× overbet entry is wrong: caller needs 66.7% equity, defender's MDF is 33.3%. The other three rows match the table.
